title: Salaspils unveils new concert hall
content:
From a Soviet-era cultural centre to a new cultural venue – the Salaspils Concert Hall now stands in the centre of Salaspils on the site of the former ‘Enerģētiķis’ cultural centre. The project was funded entirely from local authority funds. The total cost was 18.5 million euros.
Among the first musicians to perform on the new, spacious stage, accompanied by the Vidzeme Chamber Orchestra under the conductor Andris Veismanis, were singers Marija Naumova and Linda Leen, as well as the band “Musiqq”.
“I rate this concert hall very highly; a big thank you to the builders and to everyone who has worked to make this a reality here in Salaspils! It is a real pleasure and honour for me to perform here as a conductor and as the director of the Vidzeme Chamber Orchestra. (..) The atmosphere is excellent; everything is very well laid out, with thought given to the performers and the facilities for changing; there’s plenty of space. I think that, for the Salaspils district as a whole, this is one of the best concert halls in the Pieriga region that I know of. Especially for this kind of music – pop music combined with a classical orchestra sounds really good,” said Andris Veismanis, artistic director and conductor of the Vidzeme Chamber Orchestra, with delight.
“I can say that the sound is truly excellent and the stage is cosy – large and deep, which is very important. Do you know what I’m thinking of? I sang in this concert hall, in this cultural centre, some thirty years ago. It’s a huge pleasure that we have a venue like this, a cultural space like this, so close to Riga,” shared singer Marija Naumova, giving her first impressions.
Linda Leen agreed with her colleague: “It’s great that there’s another venue near Riga with new technology and a good atmosphere. I hope the venue does well and has many colourful days ahead.”

title: Evaluating functional outcomes following hand therapy in cubital tunnel release.
content: Cubital tunnel syndrome is the second most common nerve compression of the upper extremity and requires procedural intervention in nearly half of cases. Postoperative hand therapy is inconsistently utilized, and functional benefits have not been well-characterized. To investigate whether consistent therapy attendance improves postoperative functional outcomes and quantify the impact of socioeconomic factors on recovery. Retrospective chart review. Patients at a single academic institution from 2014 to 2024 with cubital tunnel syndrome treated with surgical release were reviewed. Patient demographics, postoperative clinic visits, hand therapy attendance, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System, and Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand scores were tallied. Bivariate analysis compared patients attending four or more hand therapy sessions to those who did not. The area of deprivation was used to divide patients into two halves for analysis. A total of 1396 patients were eligible for inclusion, with 461 (33.0%) attending hand therapy for 1 [1, 4] session. Among patients attending hand therapy, patients with consistent attendance had better Pain Interference, Upper Extremity Function, and subjective pain at 3 months and latest visit. Socioeconomically deprived patients had lower therapy and clinic attendance, with worse Physical Function, Pain Interference, and Upper Extremity Function 3 months postoperatively. Socioeconomic characteristics and natural functional recovery drive hand therapy engagement. In patients who require therapy, consistent attendance provided functional and pain benefits, particularly after 3 months. Poor socioeconomic status was associated with lower hand therapy attendance and worse functional outcomes.

title: 35 Years of Change: 10.7 Million Residents, New Cities and Tajikistan’s Green Course
content:
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan has changed noticeably: the population and cities have grown, the education and healthcare systems have expanded, the labor market has transformed, and issues of environmental protection and water resources have reached the international level.
Demographics
Over 35 years of independence, Tajikistan’s population has grown significantly, and the country has maintained its status as one of the states with a young demographic structure.
Since the early 1990s, the country’s population has more than doubled. According to the Agency on Statistics under the President of Tajikistan, as of January 1, 2026, the country was home to 10.721 million people. Population growth was driven by natural increase — high birth rates and increased life expectancy.
Today, young people make up a significant portion of the population. About a third of the country’s residents are children and teenagers, and the majority of the population is of working age. This demographic structure creates both opportunities for economic and labor market development, as well as new challenges in the areas of education, employment, and social infrastructure.
Life expectancy indicators have also changed over the years of independence. Improvements in the healthcare system, development of the social sector, and better living conditions have contributed to its growth compared to the early 1990s.
Demographic growth remains one of the key factors in Tajikistan’s development: the increase in the number of residents affects the demand for new jobs, housing construction, and the development of schools, medical facilities, and urban infrastructure.
Urbanization
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s cities have changed noticeably: the number of urban residents has grown, urban infrastructure has expanded, housing construction volumes have increased, and new social facilities have appeared.
From 1991 to 2026, the number of urban residents in Tajikistan increased from 1.7 million to 2.8 million people. At the same time, the share of the urban population in the country’s total population changed from 39.1% to 26.6%.
Despite the decline in share, which is associated with faster population growth in rural areas, the country’s cities took in approximately 1.1 million new residents during this period.
The capital became the prime example of urban transformation. While approximately 600,000 people lived in Dushanbe in 1991, by 2026 the city’s population had reached approximately 1.3 million residents.
Over the years of independence, the capital has expanded: new residential districts, modern roads, parks, sports, and cultural facilities have appeared.
Population growth was accompanied by an increase in construction volumes.
In January–June 2026, the volume of commissioned housing amounted to 802,900 square meters, which is 1.5 times more than during the same period of the previous year.
Over 35 years, new roads and interchanges, bridges and overpasses, schools, kindergartens, universities, medical facilities, parks, recreational areas, sports, and cultural facilities have appeared in the country’s cities.
The development of urban infrastructure has become one of the key areas of transformation in Tajikistan’s cities.
Education
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s education system has expanded significantly. The network of general education institutions has grown, the number of students and teachers has increased, and opportunities for vocational and higher education have expanded.
During this period, new schools, colleges, and universities have appeared, children’s enrollment in education has grown, and the number of young people obtaining a specialty and higher education has increased noticeably.
Special attention is paid to the development of preschool education, the training of teaching staff, and the establishment of new educational institutions.
Changes in the education system reflect the country’s population growth and the growing need for accessible and quality education for new generations.
Healthcare
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s healthcare system has expanded significantly: the number of medical facilities has increased, the number of doctors and mid-level medical personnel has grown, and opportunities for providing medical care to the population have expanded.
The development of the sector was accompanied by the construction and modernization of medical facilities, personnel training, and the strengthening of healthcare infrastructure.
Changes in the system reflect the growing demand of the population for medical services and the drive to improve the accessibility and quality of medical care.
Work and Employment
Over the years of independence, the labor market has undergone significant changes: the number of people employed in the economy has grown, labor resources have increased, and the structure of employment has changed.
The country’s economy gradually transitioned from a predominantly agrarian model to a more diverse structure, in which the service sector and industry play an increasingly important role.
At the same time, the directions of employment changed: the share of those working in agriculture declined, while the number of people employed in the service sector and other sectors of the economy increased.
The growth of labor resources has become one of the main factors in the country’s economic development, creating new challenges and opportunities for the labor market, including the need to create jobs and develop professional skills.
Environment
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan has expanded its nature conservation system, reduced pollutant emissions, and become a participant in international environmental initiatives.
During this period, the area of specially protected natural territories grew more than sevenfold — from 420,000 hectares in 1991 to 3.1 million hectares in 2025. Today, approximately 22% of the country’s territory is occupied by nature reserves, national parks, and other conservation zones.
One of the important areas of environmental policy has been the preservation of the country’s unique natural ecosystems — mountain landscapes, glaciers, and rare species of animals and plants.
Over the years of independence, emissions of pollutants from stationary sources have also decreased significantly. While their volume was 656,800 tons in 1991, in 2024 it was 129,900 tons, which is almost five times less.
Tajikistan is actively promoting the environmental agenda at the international level. On the initiative of the country, the UN declared the International Decade “Water for Life” (2005–2015), the Decade of Action “Water for Sustainable Development” (2018–2028), and 2025 as the International Year of Glacier Preservation.
Today, environmental challenges remain among the country’s top priorities: climate change, glacier retreat, water resource conservation, and biodiversity protection require ongoing efforts.

title: Genomic Research as a Critical Pathway to Diagnosis for Individuals with Rare Disease
content: Many individuals with rare monogenic disease remain molecularly undiagnosed due to challenges accessing genetic testing, ambiguity in interpretation of uncertain variants, and latency between novel disease-gene discovery and adoption into clinical pipelines. The Rare Genomes Project (RGP) provides a remote, research-based genomic sequencing (GS) service for rare disease families to overcome diagnostic barriers while advancing the understanding of the genetic basis of rare disease. Short-read GS and family-centered analysis were performed to identify causes of primary disease. Variants meeting return criteria were clinically confirmed and returned to families. Since 2017, RGP enrolled clinically heterogeneous, undiagnosed rare disease families from all fifty states, Washington DC, and Puerto Rico. Findings were returned to 272 of 1014 sequenced families, resulting in a solve rate of 23.3% and a returned strong candidate rate of 3.5%. Condition-specific return rates ranged from 15% to 40% with many families receiving a result in a known disease gene after healthcare access challenges. Research interventions contributed to returns in 16% of all families and included variants in recently discovered or non-coding disease genes, additional functional studies to resolve variant uncertainty, and real-time data sharing to empower novel disease-gene discovery. RGP demonstrates that a research-based, patient-driven remote sequencing study can effectively bridge a diagnostic gap for rare disease families underserved in current clinical care. This study also underscores the clinical utility of GS with frequent re-analysis and highlights the critical continued role of research in variant interpretation, method innovation, and genomic knowledge base expansion for rare disease diagnosis.

title: Students turn waste into runway-worthy fashion at TVET Expo 2026
content:

(Kaieteur News) – Creativity took centre stage on Wednesday as students from secondary schools across Guyana transformed discarded and recyclable materials into striking fashion pieces during the ‘Trash to Fashion Show’, one of the featured activities of the TVET Expo & Fair 2026.
Held at the Arthur Chung Convention Centre under the theme “Recycle. Reinvent. Runway.”, the showcase challenged students to rethink the possibilities of materials that are often considered waste and demonstrate how creativity, technical skills and innovation can come together to create something new.
The Trash to Fashion Show featured four categories: Casual Wear (Recycled Chic), Professional/Career Wear, Creative/Avant-Garde, and Cultural/Themed Wear. Students were tasked with designing and presenting outfits made using recycled, reused or discarded materials.
The runway featured an impressive display of creativity, with students incorporating sustainability into fashion while showcasing their individual design concepts and stage presence.
In the Casual/Recycled Chic category, Melina Moe of Friendship Secondary School captured first place with “Rise of the Golden Arrowhead,” while Quecia Joseph of New Central High School placed second with “Pages in Motion.”
The Professional/Career Wear category was won by Shaddai Scipio of North Georgetown Secondary School with “Clock It.”
In the Creative/Avant-Garde category, Destiny Hytmiah of Christ Church Secondary School secured first place with “Reclaim Royalty,” while Onella Lepps of Buxton Secondary School took second place with “The Delicious Fit.”
North Georgetown Secondary School also dominated the Cultural/Themed Wear category, with Tyfeia Torrington taking first place for “Ofishka” and Atarah Hart securing second place with “Lokono (Beauty).”
The showcase also featured guest participant Atiena Chester, who presented “Eco Alliance” in the Cultural category.
Beyond the category awards, several students were recognised for outstanding elements of their designs. Melina Moe received the awards for Best Overall Design, Most Wearable Design and Best Stage Presence, while Destiny Hytmiah earned Most Creative Outfit, Best Use of Recycled Materials and Best Transformation.
TVET continues to provide students with opportunities to move beyond theory and apply their skills through practical, creative and hands-on experiences.
Through initiatives such as the Trash to Fashion Show, students are encouraged to see technical and vocational education not simply as classroom learning, but as a pathway for developing creativity, problem-solving, entrepreneurship and skills that can be applied in the world of work.

title: Umbau fast fertig - Guter Ruf der Schule hat auch Bayern erreicht
content:
Nach dreijährigem Bauzeit und Kosten von rund 41 Millionen Euro ist der Umbau des ABZ Waizenkirchen fast fertig. Der Schulbetrieb läuft wieder uneingeschränkt. 55 Lehrer unterrichten in der Kaderschmiede für Landwirte 500 Schüler, die nicht nur aus Region kommen.
Seit fast einem Jahrhundert hat in Waizenkirchen die landwirtschaftliche Ausbildung Tradition. Zunächst am Marktplatz, seit den 1960er Jahren steht die Kaderschmiede für angehende Landwirte an der Ortsgrenze. Im Mittelpunkt stand in den letzten drei Jahren der Umbau des Agrarbildungszentrums. Insgesamt flossen rund 41 Millionen Euro in die Modernisierung von Internat, Schule und Werkstättentrakt.
„Das Gebäude verläuft entlang einer 180 Meter langen Wirbelsäule und umfasst eine Nutzfläche von rund 8000 Quadratmetern“, verriet Alois Aigner von der Landesimmobiliengesellschaft LH Thomas Stelzer und Agrarlandesrätin Michaela Langer-Weninger (beide VP) bei einem Rundgang.
„Bald beginnt die letzte Phase des Projekts. Der bestehende Standort der Fachschule wird abgetragen. Im Frühjahr werden die Außenanlagen fertiggestellt“, fügte Direktor Walter Raab hinzu. Er führte die Gäste in die Werkstätten, wo genäht, gehobelt oder Blumensträuße gebunden wurden. Philip Heindl von der 1c-Klasse stellte seine Kreativität beim Holzbearbeiten unter Beweis. Er kommt aus Hutthurm bei Passau. „Mein Opa ist Forstwirt und von Freunden habe ich vom guten Ruf der Schule erfahren. Der erste Eindruck ist super“, so der 15-Jährige.

title: Ko dom postane prostor oskrbe: kaj je dobro vedeti, ko skrbite za bližnjega?
content:
V želji, da bi njihov bližnji čim dlje ostal doma in hkrati prejemal kakovostno oskrbo, se zgodbe številnih družinskih oskrbovalcev začnejo podobno. Sprva gre za pomoč pri nakupih, spremstvo k zdravniku ali pripravo obrokov. Sčasoma pa se lahko pojavijo še težave z gibljivostjo, osebno higieno, demenca in inkontinenca. Takrat dom nenadoma postane prostor polne oskrbe.
S tem pa pridejo tudi vprašanja: Kako organizirati nego, ko sem v službi, po opravkih? Kako preprečiti zaplete? Kje poiskati pomoč? In kako ob vseh obveznostih poskrbeti tudi zase?
Domača oskrba je danes resničnost številnih slovenskih družin. Po podatkih Inštituta Antona Trstenjaka za gerontologijo in medgeneracijsko sožitje doma nekoga oskrbuje več kot 300.000 ljudi, družinski oskrbovalci pa zagotovijo približno 80 odstotkov vse oskrbe.
Skrb za bližnjega ni le fizično zahtevna, ampak lahko pomeni tudi čustveno in organizacijsko obremenitev. Zato je pomembno, da se o oskrbi bližnjega družina temeljito pogovori in pridobi čim več informacij. Viri informacij in podpore so lahko:
V okviru sistema dolgotrajne oskrbe lahko upravičenci koristijo različne oblike podpore, med drugim oskrbovalca družinskega člana, dolgotrajno oskrbo na domu, e-oskrbo ter storitve za ohranjanje in krepitev samostojnosti.
Več o pravicah in storitvah dolgotrajne oskrbe si lahko preberete na tej povezavi. Na voljo je tudi klicni center na številki 114, kjer lahko vsak delovni dan med 8. in 16. uro dobite preverjene in celovite informacije o dolgotrajni oskrbi.
Med najpogostejšimi izzivi, s katerimi se srečujejo družinski oskrbovalci, je tudi inkontinenca.
Ne glede na to, ali gre za uhajanje urina ali dvojno inkontinenco (uhajanje urina in blata), lahko ta pomembno vpliva na kakovost življenja uporabnika in njegovih bližnjih. Poleg same izbire ustreznega pripomočka je treba poskrbeti tudi za redno higieno, zaščito kože in čim večje udobje uporabnika.
Prav nega in skrb za kožo sta za oskrbovalce večji izziv, kot so pričakovali. Zaradi dolgotrajne izpostavljenosti trenju in dražečim snovem v izločkih se poveča tveganje za nastanek inkontinenčnega dermatitisa (IAD), ene najpogostejših težav oseb z inkontinenco.
Pri dolgotrajni oskrbi pogosto velja, da največjo razliko naredijo majhni vsakodnevni koraki.
Strokovnjaki zato za nego kože oseb z inkontinenco priporočajo preprost pristop v treh korakih:
Pomembno je, da izberete pripomoček za inkontinenco s hitro vpojnostjo, ki površino, kjer se vpojno jedro stika s kožo, ohranja suho in je izdelan iz zračnih materialov. Pomembno je, da pripomoček omogoča zračenje kože in tako podpira njeno naravno ravnovesje.
Ob menjavi pripomočka za inkontinenco je pomembno nežno in temeljito očistiti kožo. Pri tem je priporočljivo uporabljati izdelke, namenjene za občutljivo kožo, ki čistijo brez nepotrebnega draženja. Najpriročnejši so izdelki za čiščenje kože, ki jih ni treba izpirati z vodo.
Z leti postaja koža tanjša in občutljivejša. Redna uporaba negovalnih izdelkov, kot so vlažilne kreme in losjoni, pomaga ohranjati njeno prožnost in zmanjšuje izsušenost.
Na predelih, ki so pogosto izpostavljeni vlagi, pa posebna mazila ustvarijo dodatno zaščito med kožo in dražečimi dejavniki ter pomagajo zmanjšati možnost poškodb kože.
Ta pristop temelji na sistemu treh korakov za preprečevanje inkontinenčnega dermatitisa, ki ga uporabljajo tudi številni strokovnjaki v zdravstveni in socialni oskrbi.
Kateri izdelek za čiščenje in nego kože izbrati? Vprašajte digitalnega pomočnika.
Če niste prepričani, kateri izdelek izbrati, vam je lahko v pomoč brezplačno orodje danskega podjetja ABENA, ki na podlagi odgovorov na nekaj preprostih vprašanj o negi pripravi izbor izdelkov za čiščenje in nego kože. Preizkusite ga lahko na tej povezavi.
Pogost razlog za nelagodje, iztekanje ali draženje kože ni nujno stopnja inkontinence, ampak uporaba neustreznega pripomočka, lahko tudi njegova neustrezna namestitev.
Pri izbiri je treba upoštevati:
Ker je izdelkov za inkontinenco veliko, je odločitev pogosto zahtevna. O izbiri se lahko pogovorite z osebnim zdravnikom, ki lahko glede na stopnjo inkontinence predpiše pripomočke za inkontinenco tudi z naročilnico za medicinske pripomočke, ali s farmacevtom v lekarni. Na voljo pa je tudi brezplačno orodje, ki na podlagi vaših odgovorov pripravi nabor pripomočkov.
Skrb za bližnjega doma je lahko ena najlepših oblik medsebojne podpore. Hkrati pa je to odgovornost, ki prinaša številne nove naloge, znanja in odločitve.
Zato največ štejejo preverjene informacije, strokovni nasveti in pripomočki, ki olajšajo vsakdan.
Ko je nega v domačem okolju dobro organizirana, koža ustrezno zaščitena in pomoč na dosegu roke, ostane več časa za tisto, kar je zares pomembno: za pogovor, bližino in občutek varnosti.

title: Free rail travel extended to bereaved military families this Remembrance weekend
content:
Free rail travel extended to bereaved military families this Remembrance weekend
Bereaved military family members will be able to travel by train free of charge this Remembrance weekend, helping them attend services and commemorative events to honour loved ones who died while serving in the Armed Forces.
Hundreds of bereaved military family members will be able to travel by train free of charge this Remembrance weekend (7-8 November), helping them attend memorial services and commemorative events to honour loved ones who died while serving in the Armed Forces.
For the first time, one next of kin of a service person who died while serving will be able to travel free of charge on National Rail services to attend Remembrance weekend events.
The move builds on the existing free travel offer for serving personnel and veterans, giving people breathing space and ensuring travel costs are not a barrier for families taking part in remembrance and reflection.
Minister for Veterans and People, Calvin Bailey, said:
“Remembrance is an opportunity for the nation to come together in recognition of the service and sacrifice of our Armed Forces. For bereaved families, this is a deeply personal time.
“We must never forget that behind every name we remember is a family whose lives have been changed forever. Providing free rail travel will help bereaved relatives come together and honour their loved one without financial barriers.”
Mikki Brett, the widow of the late CPO Stuart Brett, who served in the Weapons Engineering branch of the Royal Navy and died in service in April 2023, spoke with Minister Bailey this week. She said:
“It’s fantastic news that the in-service bereaved have been recognised for the support given to their loved ones with free train fares to remembrance events this year.”
Mikki is already registered to come to the Cenotaph on Remembrance Sunday, and will benefit directly from the new travel offer for those bereaved in service.
A spokesperson for SSAFA, the Armed Forces charity said:
“SSAFA welcomes the Department for Transport’s decision to extend free travel to bereaved military families during the Remembrance weekend.
“This change ensures that those who have lost loved ones in the service of their nation can travel to pay their respects without facing financial strain. It is a deeply meaningful gesture that properly honours the sacrifices of our Forces families ensuring they can stand together with the nation in remembrance.”
How to apply for free travel
Eligible family members wishing to take up the offer have until 16 October to apply for a free ticket through the Defence Medical Welfare Service.
Support following a military bereavement
Remembrance can be a particularly significant time for those grieving the death of someone who served in the Armed Forces. While commemorations can bring comfort, they can also bring difficult emotions and memories.
Cruse Bereavement Support offers a dedicated Military Bereavement service, funded by the Armed Forces Covenant Fund Trust, for anyone grieving the death of a serving member of the Armed Forces who died in service, or an ex-serving person who died due to service-attributable reasons.
Support is available across England and Wales for family members, partners, friends, colleagues and anyone affected by the loss, at any time after the bereavement.

title: L’Azerbaïdjan gracie le Français emprisonné Martin Ryan, par décret présidentiel
content:
20 Minutes avec AFP
Un nouveau succès pour la diplomatie française. L’Azerbaïdjan a gracié ce mercredi Martin Ryan, un Français emprisonné dans ce pays du Caucase depuis fin 2023.
La décision intervient quelques heures après la levée des sanctions européennes visant l’oligarque russe Alicher Ousmanov que demandait la France.
Selon un décret du président azerbaïdjanais Ilham Aliev publié mercredi, Martin Ryan figure dans une liste de 20 personnes graciées et est le seul ressortissant français à en bénéficier.
Un accord de libération
Selon un diplomate à Bruxelles, Paris a fait pression auprès des pays membres de l’UE pour lever les sanctions visant Alicher Ousmanov dans le cadre d’un accord de libération de prisonniers impliquant des citoyens français détenus en Azerbaïdjan. La France n’a jamais confirmé de telles tractations, mais réclame depuis des mois la libération de l’homme d’affaires Martin Ryan, condamné à dix ans de prison pour « espionnage » en mars 2026.
Installé à Bakou depuis plusieurs années, Martin Ryan avait été arrêté le 4 décembre 2023 par les autorités azerbaïdjanaises, l’accusant d' « espionnage » au profit des services secrets français. Le ministère français des Affaires étrangères a toujours rejeté « catégoriquement » ces accusations, qualifiant cette détention d'« arbitraire ».
Un autre Français encore emprisonné
Selon l’accusation, Martin Ryan aurait collecté des informations concernant les relations de l’Azerbaïdjan avec la Turquie, l’Iran et le Pakistan, concernant des entreprises liées à la Russie et à la Chine et sur des questions stratégiques régionales liées au Karabakh. Son procès avait débuté en janvier 2025 à Bakou mais ce n’est que plus d’un an plus tard, le 16 mars dernier, qu’il avait été condamné. Un coaccusé azerbaïdjanais, Azad Mamedli, avait été, lui, condamné à douze ans de prison pour « haute trahison ».
Selon le décret présidentiel publié mercredi, outre Martin Ryan, quatre autres ressortissants étrangers figurent parmi les personnes libérées : un Russe, un Pakistanais et deux Turcs. Un autre citoyen français est emprisonné en Azerbaïdjan, l’homme d’affaires Anass Derraz. Il a été condamné à douze ans de prison en novembre 2025 à Bakou dans une affaire où il est accusé d’avoir accepté un pot-de-vin d’un oligarque russe.
Relations tendues
Les relations bilatérales entre la France et l’Azerbaïdjan se sont fortement dégradées après la reprise par Bakou, en septembre 2023, du contrôle du territoire du Karabakh, alors à majorité arménienne, ce qui a provoqué le déplacement de plus de 100.000 habitants.
Bakou reprochait le soutien de Paris à l’Arménie. Les autorités françaises ont accusé en retour l’Azerbaïdjan d’une ingérence concernant ses territoires d’outre-mer, ce que Bakou nie.

title: Burkina Faso: From Cotton to Uniforms, Burkina Faso Boosts its Textile Industry
content:
By introducing traditional fabrics into school, judicial and military uniforms, as well as some public-service attire, Burkina Faso is seeking to create a sustainable market for locally processed cotton. The policy could support spinning mills, women weavers and garment workshops, provided the sector can meet the required volumes, prices and deadlines.
In a small workshop equipped with two looms in the Taabtenga neighbourhood of Ouagadougou, Véronique Thiombiano Yonli and her colleagues are working hard to finish a length of cloth due the following day.
It is cencingu, also known as Tchintchingou in French, a fabric of Gourmantché origin deeply rooted in the traditions of eastern Burkina Faso.

The fabric gained national prominence when the government selected it for the parade uniform worn on 25 July 2026 at the graduation ceremony for the 25th class of active-duty officer cadets from the Georges Namoano Military Academy in Pô, about 140 kilometres from Ouagadougou.
Behind the cultural significance of the uniform lies a broader economic objective. By expanding the use of traditional fabrics, particularly Faso Dan Fani, across the public service and in schools, courts and the military, the state is stimulating demand for textiles produced in the country. The orders could support spinning mills, dyers, women weavers and garment workshops, while retaining more of the value generated by Burkina Faso’s cotton within the country.
The state creates a market for local fabrics
Since Captain Ibrahim Traoré came to power in 2022, the government has introduced a series of measures to promote Burkinabè fabrics. Following a national forum on Faso Dan Fani in May 2023, a decree adopted the next month encouraged the wearing and use of Faso Dan Fani, Koko Dunda and other traditional fabrics in the public service, at official ceremonies and in the decoration of public buildings.
The measure was subsequently extended to schools. During a pilot phase in the 2025–2026 school year, pupils in four municipalities wore Faso Dan Fani or Koko Dunda uniforms twice a week. The government said the trial was not compulsory but plans to roll out the policy more widely from the start of the 2026–2027 school year. The details have yet to be specified.
In October 2024, Faso Dan Fani also became the courtroom attire of magistrates and court clerks. Orders from the defence and security forces and other public institutions have added to this demand. Together, these decisions are gradually turning uniforms and official attire into markets for local textiles.
The challenge of producing parade uniforms
Abdoul Ben Isaac Compaoré, a garment engineer and founder of the Black brand, made the officer cadets’ parade uniforms. The order tested his workshop. “We had to make 252 suits in four weeks,” he says, describing it as “a suicide mission that we had to pull off — and we did.”
According to Compaoré, the made-to-measure suits were produced through an entirely Burkinabè supply chain. “The yarn comes from FILSAH. The fabrics were produced by women weavers I brought in from different places, the other accessories were also made locally, and I contributed the design,” he says.
For producers, the appeal of this market lies in both its volume and its regularity. Its impact, however, depends on how contracts are awarded and whether local-content requirements are enforced. If the yarn or fabric is imported, a significant share of the value still escapes the national economy.
Tailor Soumanou Kiéma believes the state should also organise trade fairs to raise awareness of Faso Dan Fani. “Public orders must be more regular,” he says.
He also calls for stronger training for women weavers to ensure the quality of the fabrics.
FILSAH seeks markets for its yarn
The local-uniform policy comes as Burkina Faso seeks to process more of its cotton domestically. Based in Bobo-Dioulasso, the Filature du Sahel, or FILSAH, is experiencing renewed activity after several difficult years.
The company, representing an investment of 18.5 billion CFA francs (US$32.7 million), turns cotton fibre into yarn supplied mainly to women weavers and producers of traditional cloth. At an open day on 30 April 2026, managing director Abdoulaye Nabolé announced an annual capacity of 10,000 tonnes of yarn and about 550 direct jobs, figures confirmed by the Ministry of Commerce.
According to Nabolé, the cotton-textile value chain “accounts for more than 10% of gross domestic product and supports more than 3.5 million people”.
But production capacity does not guarantee a market. FILSAH says fraudulent imports of yarn and cloth weakened its operations, contributing to unsold stock worth as much as three billion CFA francs (US$5.3 million). In 2026, enforcement agencies announced the seizure of fraudulent or illegally imported textile products valued at several hundred million CFA francs.
Public procurement could therefore support yarn manufactured by FILSAH. Its effect will nevertheless depend on the company’s ability to deliver the required quantities at competitive prices and within the prescribed deadlines.
Demand reaches the workshops
For some women weavers, the effects are already visible. Thiombiano Yonli says the promotion of traditional cloth has revived her business. “I have never seen my workshop this busy since I started this trade in 2020,” she says.
With only two looms, she sometimes manages “to weave as many as two lengths of cloth a day”. She received orders from schools at the start of the 2025–2026 school year and hopes the demand will continue.
Her prices vary according to the weight of the fabric, the yarn and the dye. “My cloth costs between 4,000 and 8,000 CFA francs, taking the economic situation into account so that I can keep my customers,” she explains. She says she no longer uses imported yarn: “With the state’s commitment to promoting traditional cloth, I now source 100% Burkinabè yarn from FILSAH.”
Her experience illustrates the intended mechanism: a school order provides work for the workshop and, further up the supply chain, creates demand for locally produced yarn.
In Loumbila, Alizèta Ouoba Nikiéma runs the Faso Impact training centre with her husband. She estimates that its turnover reached about 10 million CFA francs (US$17,700) over the past year, compared with approximately five million CFA francs two years earlier. She attributes the growth to the promotion of traditional fabrics, as well as to the rigour of their work.
“At Faso Impact, we weave all kinds of traditional cloth, including Faso Dan Fani, cencingu, Mandili and many others,” she explains. The work also requires mastery of dyeing because FILSAH’s yarn is sold white.
The National Federation of Women Weavers of Burkina Faso, FENATI/BF, has delivered 1,200 lengths of cloth worth 12 million CFA francs (US$21,200). In a report presented on 8 May 2026, it also cited its contribution to the production of Faso Dan Fani school uniforms.
Production capacity put to the test
Rising demand creates opportunities but also exposes the sector’s constraints. Thiombiano Yonli lacks the means to buy additional looms. At Faso Impact, cramped dormitories prevent the centre from accepting more trainees.
“My centre serves a social purpose. Most of the trainees have fled conflict zones or forced marriage,” says Nikiéma, who is calling for additional facilities.
The government is attempting to address some of these constraints by building the National Centre for the Support of Artisanal Cotton Processing, known as CNATAC. Built on a 10-hectare site, it is intended to bring together weaving, dyeing, cutting and sewing workshops, as well as training and exhibition spaces. The project could help artisans fulfil larger orders and meet common standards for quality and delivery times.
Progress remains uneven, however. In Fada N’Gourma and Ziniaré, Tanilemba Tankoano and Viviane Dayamba Bouda are still struggling to sell their cloth. Bouda sells only two pieces a week, earning an estimated profit of between 2,000 and 3,000 CFA francs (US$3.50–US$5.30). Her workshop, situated inside a large welding yard, has little visibility. She does not belong to an association and has no presence on social media.
Tankoano, meanwhile, did not consider weaving her main occupation until government policy encouraged her to invest more in it. The contrast with workshops receiving school orders shows that access to public contracts, equipment, finance, raw materials and commercial networks remains decisive.
From public procurement to industry
Alongside FILSAH and CNATAC, the government is developing TEXFORCES-BF, a textile complex intended to supply clothing to the defence and security forces as well as the wider population. It was inaugurated on 9 September.
These projects reflect the ambition to connect cotton production to spinning, weaving and, ultimately, the manufacture of finished garments. The challenge now is to turn uniform policies into sustainable, measurable orders that genuinely use Burkinabè cotton and yarn, while ensuring that small businesses and women weavers’ associations can access them.
For workshops such as Thiombiano Yonli’s, the initial effects are visible. But moving from a growing number of artisanal orders to a fully fledged textile industry will depend on Burkina Faso’s ability to organise the entire value chain, from cotton grown in its fields to uniforms worn in its schools and institutions.

title: « Mon dossier s’était perdu dans les limbes de la CAF » : le grand saut administratif vers l’âge adulte
content:
Assise avec une amie devant son dossier de la MDPH (Maison départementale des personnes handicapées), une vingtaine de pages posées sur la table, Adèle (les personnes citées par un simple prénom ont requis l’anonymat), 26 ans, prend une grande inspiration. A côté d’elle, son classeur médical, épais d’une dizaine de centimètres, est grand ouvert. Elle y cherche des résultats d’IRM, des comptes rendus de consultation, des arrêts maladie… Mais le plus difficile reste de comprendre ce qu’on attend d’elle.
Que faut-il écrire dans ce grand carré bleu « Vie quotidienne » ? Les conséquences de son endométriose et de sa fibromyalgie ? Et si elles fluctuent ? Les consignes ne sont pas claires. « Une assistante sociale m’avait juste dit de cocher les cases, alors qu’il fallait détailler chaque symptôme et leur fréquence. J’ai dû tout refaire ! », dit-elle dans un souffle.
Sa première demande, déposée en 2024, est refusée : des documents médicaux manquent. Dix mois plus tard, en juillet 2025, elle obtient finalement une allocation mensuelle de 1 033 euros. Entre-temps, Adèle a dû continuer à travailler dans la vente malgré ses douleurs : « Ça m’a forcément abîmé la santé encore un peu plus ! » Au total, le manque à gagner s’élève à près « d’une dizaine de milliers d’euros ».

title: Fußball spielender Pfarrer: Der Elfmeterheld mit Verbindung nach ganz oben
content:
Johann Wurzer ist Pfarrer in der österreichischen Gemeinde Opponitz – und spielt in seiner Freizeit leidenschaftlich Fußball. Als kürzlich der Torhüter beim SV Opponitz ausgefallen ist, half der 64 Jahre alte Wurzer aus. Ein echter Glücksfall für den Verein, denn er hielt einen Elfmeter und verhalf der Reserve des SV Opponitz zum Auswärtssieg gegen den des FCU Strengberg in der Liga. Ein Anruf bei einem Priester, der von Berufs wegen auch bei internationalen Turnieren antritt.
SZ: Herr Wurzer, wann haben Sie erfahren, dass Sie von der Kirche ins Fußballtor wechseln sollen?
Johann Wurzer: Der Trainer hat mich am Abend vor dem Spiel gefragt. Beim Training. Ich bin ja kein Stammspieler beim SV Opponitz, trainiere aber regelmäßig mit der Mannschaft.
Was war Ihre erste Reaktion?
Innere Freude darüber, dass ich in meinem Alter überhaupt bei Spielen mitwirken kann.
Mit ihren 64 Jahren sind sie wohl sehr fit.
Zur Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft haben wir eine Messe veranstaltet. Das ist für mich als Fußballer Pflicht. Im Anschluss durften die Gottesdienstteilnehmer ins Elfmeterschießen gegen mich. 67 Leute sind angetreten, da bin ich ungefähr 140 Mal auf den Boden geflogen.
Den Körpereinsatz haben Sie auch beim Spiel gegen den SV Strengberg gezeigt. Zwischenzeitlich führte Ihre Mannschaft mit 3:1. Als der Schiedsrichter einen Elfmeter für die Gegner gepfiffen hat, haben Sie da gebetet?
Nein, ich habe den Elfmeterschützen genau beobachtet. Er hat ins linke Eck geschaut und die rechte Hand beim Ablegen vorn gehabt. Das hieß für mich, er möchte in diese Ecke schießen. Zweimal hat er dieses ziemlich eindeutige Zeichen gemacht. Ich hatte recht.
War Ihnen dabei auch Ihre innere Verbindung nach ganz oben hilfreich?
Ich würde eher sagen, das ist die Routine, wenn man über 50 Jahre Torwart ist.
Sie haben den Elfer gehalten, sodass Ihre Mannschaft am Ende das Spiel gewonnen hat.
Eine Sensation! Wir haben eineinhalb Jahre nicht mehr mit der Reserve gewonnen. Das haben wir auch gefeiert und da habe ich auch wohl einen guten Teil von dem gesponserten Bier mitgetrunken.
Aber hoffentlich nicht zu viel, Sie mussten ja am Wochenende noch arbeiten.
Ich musste am folgenden Tag erst am Abend die Samstagsmesse halten. Da hatte ich noch ein bisschen Zeit, mich von der Siegesfeier zu erholen.
Nebenbei spielen Sie auch für die Priesternationalmannschaft in Österreich.
Ja, es gibt jedes Jahr Europameisterschaften, da nehmen meistens 18 Mannschaften teil. Die nächste ist in Priština, in Kosovo. Und jeder muss halt schauen, dass er sich bis dahin fit hält.
Wie schlagen sich denn die österreichischen Pfarrer dabei?
Ich sage immer, wir sind ziemlich die Besten vom letzten Drittel. Polen, Kroatien und Portugal machen seit Jahren den Sieg unter sich aus.
Woran liegt das, weniger Sünden?
In Polen finden zum Beispiel in einem Jahr so viele Priesterweihen statt wie in Österreich in zehn Jahren. Die könnten wahrscheinlich jedes Jahr eine neue Mannschaft aufstellen.
Spielen Priester eigentlich fairer als andere Fußballer?
Nein, sie werden von genau so viel Ehrgeiz und der Fanatismus angetrieben wie andere Sportler. Da wird ebenso psychologisch gearbeitet und optimiert.
Was ist für Sie eigentlich schwieriger: Einen Elfmeter zu halten oder genügend Besucher in die Kirche zu locken?
Eine volle Kirche. Ich betreue drei Pfarreien. In einer davon kommen sehr viele junge Familien und Jugendliche in die Kirche. In den anderen beiden eher nicht. Woran das liegt, weiß ich leider auch nicht.
Jetzt, wo Sie so bekannt sind, kommen vielleicht wieder mehr Menschen?
Vielleicht. Das wäre schön.

title: Immigration Lawyer John Dutton Frees Cuban from 'Death Row' Detention Center
content:
Walter Carmenate Paradela, a Cuban holding permanent residency in the United States, has walked free from the Bluebonnet detention center—referred to by inmates as "death row"—without paying a single dollar in bail, all thanks to the dedicated efforts of the Houston-based John Dutton Law Firm.
Describing his release with disbelief, Walter Carmenate shared, "I'm the second person to leave that center. Someone else got out first, but they had to pay $40,000 in bail. I walked out without any bail; I'm just free. No one could believe it, not even the officers there thought I would leave without paying a cent."
The Unexpected Turn of Events
The trouble began with a minor traffic violation related to a car license from Florida that Walter had not yet updated in Houston. The situation worsened when he provided the court with all the vehicle's documentation, which belonged to a friend who had given him fake insurance. An earlier attorney, who represented him in that matter, advised him to plead guilty, falsely assuring him there would be no immigration repercussions—a grave mistake in hindsight.
Walter Carmenate was eventually arrested on July 27, 2026, during a meeting with his new parole officer in Amarillo, Texas. He was transported, shackled at the feet, hands, and waist, in a van for nearly four hours to the Bluebonnet facility in Anson, Texas, where he spent 51 grueling days. "Those 51 days were the hardest for me," he recounted. "I felt as if I had been there for over a year."
"You know what they call that place: death row. Nobody escapes from there. Everyone gets deported," he said.
Legal Maneuvers That Led to Freedom
Attorney John Dutton detailed the strategy that led to his client's release and the retention of his green card. According to Dutton, securing a habeas corpus in Bluebonnet is particularly challenging due to its location in the Northern District of Texas, a federal jurisdiction with few precedents favorable to immigrants.
The legal breakthrough came by pinpointing the actual date of Walter's entry into the U.S., placing him outside the five-year period the Department of Homeland Security cited for deportation. This technicality could not be disputed by the government, prompting the judge to close the case without imposing bail.
When asked about his gratitude, Walter Carmenate was quick to express his deepest appreciation: "I'm thankful to the lawyers, but especially to my wife, who was always there, never leaving me alone."
Support and Testimonies
An office client named Alexandra also shared her experience during the interview: "I am a witness to their results and especially to the heart with which this wonderful team works. I experienced firsthand their dedication, commitment, and support during one of the toughest times in my life." Dutton humbly replied, "We strive to do our job as best as we can."
Walter Carmenate's ordeal highlights a recurring pattern among Cuban permanent residents detained by ICE: minor criminal records, sometimes stemming from poor legal advice, triggering retroactive deportation proceedings in an increasingly restrictive immigration climate.
As the interview concluded, Dutton issued a caution for those with asylum cases on appeal before the BIA: they must timely pay the annual $102 fee to prevent their cases from being dismissed. The lawyer also advises eligible permanent residents to pursue citizenship promptly as a primary legal shield against such processes.
Walter Carmenate's case is just one among many illustrating the complex immigration landscape in the United States. Stay informed on detentions, bails, and immigrant rights in our U.S. Immigration section.
Key Questions on Immigration and Detention
How did Walter Carmenate secure his release without bail?
Walter Carmenate's release was secured by identifying a technicality regarding his entry date into the U.S., which placed him outside the timeframe that Homeland Security used to justify his deportation. This legal strategy led to the case being closed without bail.
What challenges exist for obtaining a habeas corpus in Bluebonnet?
Obtaining a habeas corpus in Bluebonnet is challenging because it operates under the Northern District of Texas jurisdiction, known for its limited precedents in favor of immigrants.

title: Life-extending breast cancer drug made available on the NHS after U-turn
content:
Life-extending breast cancer drug made available on the NHS after U-turn
The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) announced that it has reversed an initial decision to reject the drug for widespread use for the NHS in England
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Breast cancer patients have said they are "thrilled" after the health spending watchdog approved a life-extending drug for NHS use.
However, campaigners said that some patients living with incurable breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body have "died waiting" for Enhertu.
The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) announced it has reversed an earlier decision rejecting the treatment for widespread NHS use in England.
In 2024, it previously stated that the treatment was "not cost effective".
It has now confirmed the drug will be provided "from today" for roughly 1,000 women with HER2-low advanced breast cancer, after a "commercial solution has now been agreed".
The therapy has been available to patients in Scotland for more than two years.
It is the first licensed targeted treatment for patients with HER2-low breast cancer that cannot be removed surgically or that has spread to other parts of the body, also known as metastatic breast cancer.
Clinical trials have found that women with breast cancer who took the drug survived for around two years, compared with 17.5 months for those who had chemotherapy.
Paula Van Santen, who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer in July 2022, said that the announcement has given her a “new sense of hope”.
Mother-of-three Ms Van Santen, 51, from Banbury, said: “Today is a day I never thought I’d see.
“After years of waiting and hoping, there aren’t enough words to express how thrilled I am to see Enhertu finally approved for use on the NHS.
“Having access to this life-extending treatment brings a new sense of hope.
“It gives me the chance of seeing my daughter graduate from university, become a grandparent for the first time and simply be a mum to my children for longer as they continue to grow.
“These are life’s simple privileges that many of us take for granted, but which mean everything to me and thousands of others living with incurable metastatic breast cancer. That’s the difference a decision like this can make.”
Patient Kathryn Hulland, 48, said the decision would give her more time with her nine-year-old daughter Grace.
Ms Hulland, from Devon, was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer in 2022.
She said: “I may still be here to support my nine-year-old daughter into high school.
“When I was first diagnosed, I was told I’d be lucky to see 12 months.
“Three years later I know how important every extra month is. It’s another chance at more time with my daughter, another chance to make memories together, another month to be her mum and see her grow.
“And that’s the hope this life-extending treatment now brings, it means everything.”
Charity Breast Cancer Now hailed the announcement as “momentous”.
Claire Rowney, chief executive, said: “After more than two years of relentless campaigning, Enhertu has been recommended by Nice for use on the NHS in England for people with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer.
“This is a momentous day for thousands of people who will now have access to a drug that will give them the opportunity to gain precious extra time with loved ones. More ordinary days that become extraordinary because they were there.
“This milestone victory belongs to every person who refused to accept that access to a life-extending treatment was out of reach. For people in England, the wait for Enhertu is finally over. We must now also see Wales and Northern Ireland make Enhertu available for use on the NHS for those who need more time to live.”
She added: “Since 2024 when it was first rejected for use, thousands of people have missed out on access to Enhertu and tragically many have died. We remember with deep gratitude the women who stood alongside us and fought for this very moment.”
Nice said that a commercial solution has now been agreed for Enhertu, also know as trastuzumab deruxtecan made by Daiichi Sankyo and Astra Zeneca, following changes made to its methods as part of the UK/US Pharmaceutical Pricing Agreement.
Helen Knight, director of medicines evaluation at Nice, said: “I’m pleased that a commercial solution, alongside recent changes to Nice’s cost-effectiveness thresholds and the use of new methods for assessing quality-of-life, has meant this treatment can now be provided on the NHS.
“However, we know this decision comes too late for many families, and our thoughts are with them today. Our role is important in ensuring NHS spending on new medicines reflects the benefits they deliver while protecting valuable health resources for other essential patient services.”
Dr Anne Rigg, consultant medical oncologist and NHS England’s national specialty adviser for chemotherapy, said: “This is hugely positive news for women with secondary breast cancer who will now be offered this life-extending treatment on the NHS, giving them the opportunity for more time with their loved ones.”
Tom Keith-Roach, UK country president for AstraZeneca, said: “Today’s announcement marks a vital milestone for women in England living with HER2 low metastatic breast cancer. It brings access into line with Scotland and 26 other European countries, offering renewed hope to more than 1,000 women living with this particularly aggressive form of the disease.”

title: Police officer ordered to pay US$120 maintenance for three children
content:
Sekai Manyere
Herald reporter
The Harare Civil Court has ordered a Police officer to pay US$120 per month towards the upkeep of his three children, aged 10, eight and four, as well as 50 percent of their school fees.
The order followed an application by Ms Diana Janga, who had approached the court seeking US$300 per month in maintenance from her former husband, Titus Mashanga.
Ms Janga told the court that Mashanga was failing to provide adequately for their children. She presented a breakdown of the children’s monthly needs amounting to US$300 and told the court that she earns about US$200 per month as a vendor.
She told the court that Mr Mashanga is a police officer who earns US$320 and ZiG6 000, which he concurred with.
Ms Janga said she needed US$150 for the children’s fees. He offered to pay US$100 towards school fees and US$50 for children’s upkeep.
He told the court that he is also taking care of his mother, who stays in the rural areas. After hearing from both parties, Magistrate Ms Makonye Janemary ordered Mr Mashanga to pay US$120 per month and half of the children’s school fees.

title: Hohe Heilungschancen - „Gibt Kinder, die kommen mit Krebs auf die Welt“
content: In der aktuellen Ausgabe von „Wiener Wissen“ analysieren die Direktorinnen des St. Anna Kinderspitals, Caroline Hutter und Sabine Taschner-Mandl, den Status Quo im Bereich Kinderkrebsforschung. Taschner-Mandl: „Die Diagnostik zeigt, welche Gene betroffen sind. Eine Krebserkrankung bei Babys und Kleinkindern betrifft sogar teils auch Zellen, die nur in Embryos vorkommen.“ Hutter: „Es gibt Kinder, die kommen auf die Welt und haben schon Krebs. Natürlich ist Krebs bei Kindern eine Katastrophe. Aber es gibt in Österreich im internationalen Vergleich trotzdem gute Heilungschancen.“ Derzeit würden aufgrund der Fortschritte bei Forschung und Wissenschaft in Österreich schon rund achtzig Prozent krebsbetroffener Kinder ihre Krebserkrankung überleben. Vor dreißig Jahren seien das nur zwanzig Prozent gewesen. Ob diese Heilung dann aber auch dauerhaft sei? Hutter: „Manche Tumorzellen verstecken sich richtig. Die sieht man dann auch in der Nachbehandlung nicht.“ Es gäbe aber auch leichter erkennbare Krebsformen. Taschner-Mandl: „Ein ausgebrochener Tumor ist wie eine ungeformte Masse.“ Hutter: „Der kann auch mehrere Kilo haben. Das ist dann wie ein Knödel. Etwa im Beckenbereich kann man ihn dann auch so richtig erfühlen.“

title: Three-hour ordeal to rescue man trapped in 30-metre rock crevice
content:
Man rescued after falling down 30-metre rock crevice in San Remo, south-east of Melbourne
A man has been rescued after falling down a 30-metre rock crevice at San Remo, about 120 kilometres south-east of Melbourne.
Emergency services were called to the coastal region after reports of a man falling and becoming trapped in a rock crevice off George Bass Coastal Walk about 2:10pm on Saturday.
Emergency crews were able to communicate with the 50-year-old, who told them he had broken his leg, but they struggled to gain access to him due to the difficult terrain and rising tide.
An Ambulance Victoria helicopter was called in, with other personnel from Fire Rescue Victoria, Country Fire Authority, the State Emergency Service (SES), Air Wing, Search and Rescue Squad, Life Saving Victoria and Water Police working together to rescue the man.
Search and Rescue officers finally entered the crevice to assess him, and the man was winched to safety about 5:30pm.
He was flown to Royal Melbourne Hospital in a stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries.

title: Council spot guaranteed without election for everyone who put up their hand
content:
Candidates elected unopposed due to low nominations in Tasmanian local government elections
In short:
Two local councils in Tasmania have had fewer nominations than council seats they are trying to fill in the October local government elections.
It means a number of people have been elected unopposed.
What's next:
The period for nominations has been extended for both King Island and Tasman councils for one week in a hope to fill the roles.
Eleven people have been elected unopposed across two Tasmanian councils after they struggled to attract enough nominations ahead of next month's local government elections.
The Tasman Council received only six nominations for seven councillor positions, while the King Island Council had only five people nominate for seven available seats.
This year has seen a lower number of candidate nominations across the state compared to previous years, with 430 nominations compared to 505 four years ago.
Two hundred and eighty-three of the candidates are men, 144 are women, and 3 are non-binary.
October's elections will be the first time since the Tasmanian government reformed the number of local government council positions in the state, with 213 councillors to be elected, down from 263 previously.
Unusual but not uncommon
It's not the first time councillor roles have been filled without voters having to go to the polls.
King Island also fell short on nominations four years ago, and La Trobe council was the same in 2014.
Tasmanian Electoral Commission's Andrew Hawkey told 936 ABC Hobart there are guidelines in place for when low nominations occur.
"Under the Local Government Act, thankfully it allows us to extend the nomination period just for those vacancies," he said.
"It just gives us a bit of extra time to find those extra candidates."
Nominations opened earlier this month and closed state-wide yesterday at midday, but a week extension will be offered for King Island and Tasman councils.
While some councils struggled for numbers, others had much more interest.
Glenorchy topped the list with 12 deputy mayoral candidates while Hobart City Council has 11 in the running for mayor and 10 for deputy.
Last year, the Tasmanian government ushered in changes to the Local Government Act 1993, which will see 50 fewer councillors elected.
Only Launceston, Hobart, Clarence, Glenorchy and Kingborough will elect nine councillors, with the other 24 jurisdictions electing seven.
Starting Monday, October 5, ballot packs are set to be delivered by post, with polls closing on October 27 and counting commencing the following day.
Voting is compulsory for electors on the state roll and occurs only by ballot with no in-person polling booths available.
No hot button topics to inspire participation
Tasman Council mayor Rod MacDonald said it was disappointing to not see more nominations but put the lack of interest down to a lack of controversial issues in the region.
"There are so many different, personal reasons why they do or why they don't," he said.
"Our council's been running really well and getting things done.
"People probably were a bit more relaxed … there were no real issues to push their candidature."
All six candidates who have nominated will automatically be elected, and Cr MacDonald says he has already heard of interest in the remaining seat.
If there is one nomination, they will be elected unopposed; if there are more new candidates, they will battle it out for the final seat when ballot papers are sent out for the Tasman mayoral and deputy votes.
The Tasman council area encompasses a region east of Hobart and includes Port Arthur, Nubeena and Taranna.
Is 29 councils too many?
Tasman deputy mayor Maria Stacey will not recontest this year's local government election and said it's been a rewarding experience after three terms and twelve years in local government.
"This can be challenging at times when you do have something controversial … but it is rewarding," she said.
She says 29 councils is a lot for a small state.
"Everybody you ask thinks that 29 is too many, but they don't want their representation to be diminished; they don't want it to happen to them," she said.
"But I think eventually it will come; not in my lifetime, but it will come."

title: Court Orders Trump Administration to Bring Deported Migrant Back to U.S. from Africa
content:
A United States federal court has instructed the Trump administration to return a migrant to U.S. soil after he was deported to Africa without his consent. This ruling challenges the deportation policies to third countries that Washington has been enforcing.
On September 18, U.S. District Judge Regina M. Rodríguez from Colorado issued an order mandating the return of Bryan Omar Sánchez, a Honduran national, from the Central African Republic, where he had been sent on July 29. This occurred despite his pending asylum application and his protection under the Convention Against Torture.
"This court and many others nationwide have found that ICE's policies of expelling individuals to third countries violate the constitutional right to due process when applicants are not given notice and the chance to contest their removal before being transferred," Judge Rodríguez wrote in her decision.
Legal Challenges to Third-Country Deportations
This court ruling is part of ongoing legal battles regarding deportations to third countries. For more details on the Trump administration's immigration policies and their implications, visit our U.S. Immigration section.
Sánchez had lived in Colorado for a decade, working as a gardener, truck driver, and small pressure-washing business operator. He was apprehended by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in May 2026 and moved between detention centers in Alvarado, Texas, and Phoenix, Arizona, before being flown to Africa.
He realized his destination when he inquired with an officer on the plane. "Africa? I can't go to Africa," Sánchez reportedly stated. After nearly 22 hours of flight, he landed in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, without having consented to the transfer.
The judge not only ordered his return but also stipulated that upon arriving in Colorado, Sánchez should be "immediately released" without conditions such as GPS monitoring or periodic check-ins. He cannot be detained again unless proven, with clear evidence to an impartial judge, that he poses a flight risk or a danger to the community.
Impact of the Recent Ruling
The individual ruling concerning Sánchez comes shortly after the First Circuit Court of Appeals issued a unanimous 55-page decision declaring the Department of Homeland Security's policy of deporting migrants to third countries without prior notice or the opportunity to contest the destination as illegal.
"A person's right to challenge their removal to a country based on fear of persecution is meaningless if they do not receive prior notice of the intended destination and a meaningful opportunity to contest it," Circuit Judge Seth Aframe emphasized in the ruling.
The third-country deportation policy began on March 15, 2025, with dozens of Venezuelans being sent to the Salvadoran megaprison CECOT. Since then, Washington has signed agreements with at least 35 nations, including over a dozen African countries, to accept migrants who are not citizens of those territories.
Broader Implications and Criticisms
Among the affected immigrants are Cubans. The first deportation flight to Liberia in August 2026 included Cuban nationals among the 20 deportees. Four refused to disembark and were transferred to Equatorial Guinea, where they remained detained in a hotel in Malabo without documents or legal assistance.
Other Cubans deported to third countries have reported harsh conditions in the Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea.
Savi Arvey, the policy director at Human Rights First, described these expulsions as part of "the broader efforts by the Trump administration to undermine the global protection system and involve countries worldwide in its mass deportation campaign, which openly ignores due process and separates families."
The Trump administration is expected to appeal the First Circuit's ruling to the Supreme Court, which had temporarily permitted the continuation of these deportations while the litigation progressed.
Key Questions about U.S. Deportation Policies
What did the federal court order regarding Bryan Omar Sánchez?
The federal court ordered that Bryan Omar Sánchez be returned to the United States from the Central African Republic, where he was sent without his consent, and that he be released immediately upon arrival.
Why was the deportation policy to third countries deemed illegal?
The deportation policy was deemed illegal because it violated the constitutional right to due process by not providing migrants with notice or the opportunity to contest their removal to third countries.
How has the deportation policy affected Cuban immigrants?
Cuban immigrants have been affected by being deported to third countries like Liberia and Equatorial Guinea, facing harsh conditions and lacking legal assistance.

title: Five-year outcomes of partial breast proton beam therapy without lumpectomy for early-stage breast cancer: an interventional prospective study.
content: We report on our initial clinical experience with partial breast proton beam therapy (PB-PBT) without tumor resection as an alternative to partial mastectomy for low-risk early-stage breast cancer. This trial commenced in 2015, and eligibility criteria included women with cT1N0M0 invasive ductal carcinoma, estrogen receptor positivity, human epidermal growth factor receptor type-2 negativity, age of 40-70 years, and a performance status of 0 or 1. In Phase I, PB-PBT was administered at 62.4 Gy (RBE) in 26 fractions using the field-in-field technique. After confirming that no serious adverse events occurred, Phase II was conducted using the same dose. Follow-up evaluations were conducted every 3 months for the first year after irradiation and every 6 months thereafter. As of December 2025, 11 patients had completed a follow-up of ≥ 5 years. The median follow-up time was 82 months. Tumors exhibited immediate shrinkage post-PB-PBT, with morphological changes on ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging observed within 3-6 months. No recurrence was observed within the irradiated field in patients with > 5 years of follow-up. Dermatitis was Grade 1 in 55% of cases and Grade 2 in 45%; there were no cases of Grade ≥ 3. Grade 1 telangiectasia was observed in 36% of patients after 2 years, although most patients tolerated the treatment well. Preliminary clinical observations suggest that PB-PBT without lumpectomy achieves results within specific criteria and that it could be an option for breast cancer treatment using radiation therapy alone.

title: Dubai Mallathon concludes second edition with record turnout of more than 160,000 participants
content: Dubai: Under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, the second edition of Dubai Mallathon has concluded. Held from 15 June to 15 September, the initiative, organised by the Dubai Sports Council in collaboration with the Ministry of Defence, attracted record participation and a strong community response, strengthening its position as one of the region’s leading community sports initiatives. A total of 160,475 participants of different ages and nationalities collectively recorded more than 290 million steps across participating shopping malls and destinations. Combining physical activity with social interaction, the Dubai-wide initiative helped establish walking and running as daily habits and raised awareness of the importance of sport in improving health and quality of life. Outstanding response The second edition brought activities to more than eight malls and destinations across Dubai. Picture credit: GDMOHis Excellency Khalfan Juma Belhoul, Vice Chairman of the Dubai Sports Council, stressed that Dubai’s sports sector continues to pursue excellence through innovative community initiatives. “The response to Dubai Mallathon has been outstanding,” His Excellency said. “Professional athletes, amateur runners, beginners and families all joined in. Their enthusiasm showed how sport can bring our community together and encourage more people to get active.” Belhoul added: “The initiative’s success demonstrates our leadership’s commitment to improving quality of life in Dubai and making sport part of everyday life, helping build a healthier, happier society. With Dubai Mallathon, we are making significant progress towards achieving the goals of the Dubai Sports Sector Strategic Plan 2033. We aim to get more people exercising regularly and participating in a wider range of sporting events, helping improve health and wellbeing across our community.” He concluded: “We value the participants’ positive spirit, which reflects Dubai’s standing as one of the world’s most active cities, always moving forward and full of energy. In Dubai, we attach utmost importance to sustaining community sporting events and providing an environment that encourages physical activity throughout the year. We will continue to develop inclusive sporting activities suited to both winter and summer, ensuring that Dubai remains a leading global destination offering an integrated and sustainable sports ecosystem that meets everyone’s aspirations.” A leading initiative His Excellency Saeed Hareb, Secretary General of the Dubai Sports Council, said the initiative’s success and impressive turnout demonstrate the strength of Dubai’s sports sector and the ability of its teams to develop innovative ways to keep people active throughout the year. “Dubai Mallathon has established itself as a leading global model for translating strategic visions into tangible results,” he said. “It began in Dubai, but its message reached everyone, reinforcing the importance of making sport and physical activity part of our lives, wherever we are and whatever the season. Working closely with our partners in the government and private sectors, we successfully transformed shopping malls and major destinations into vibrant spaces for sport throughout the summer, offering a safe and comprehensive sporting experience for all members of the community.”Closing events The second edition brought activities to more than eight malls and destinations across Dubai. Dubai International Airport, Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) and Ibn Battuta Mall joined for the first time this year, alongside established partner destinations including Dubai Mall, Dubai Hills Mall, City Centre Mirdif, Mall of the Emirates, Dubai Festival City Mall and City Centre Deira. Dubai Mallathon concluded with a packed programme of activities. Dubai Hills Mall hosted a special sports and community event attended by His Excellency Khalfan Juma Belhoul, Vice Chairman of the Dubai Sports Council; Major General Khalifa Rashid Al Hamli, Director of the Office of the Minister of Defence; and several Emirati sporting legends, who joined members of the public in walking, running and community activities. The sporting legends were honoured for their achievements, participation in the initiative and role in encouraging active lifestyles. Dubai Mall also hosted a highlight of the initiative’s closing programme: a full 42.195-kilometre marathon inside the mall, alongside a 21-kilometre half-marathon, attracting record participation from professional and amateur runners. At the end of the competitions, the top finishers in both races were honoured in recognition of their outstanding performances. The three-month initiative also included more than 14 weekly races held across participating malls. Winners received valuable prizes, creating an encouraging competitive atmosphere and motivating participants to improve their performance and maintain regular exercise. The initiative also celebrated Emirati Women’s Day with dedicated events for women, including an event at Dubai Mall attended by women of different ages and backgrounds. Honouring partners The initiative also celebrated Emirati Women’s Day with dedicated events for women, including an event at Dubai Mall attended by women of different ages and backgrounds. Picture credit: GDMOThe closing events also honoured partners and supporters in recognition of their contributions to the initiative’s success. The Dubai Sports Council praised the partners’ efforts and cooperation over the three months, as well as their role in preparing venues, organising events and encouraging participation across all segments of society. Since its launch on 15 June, Dubai Mallathon attracted impressive participation from government and private sector entities, whose combined efforts helped improve the quality of life and health of employees and community members, drawing thousands of employees and their families to take an active part. Official sponsors, including Al Ameen Service, Mai Dubai, Huawei and Yango Group, also contributed to Dubai Mallathon’s success. The initiative was launched in line with the Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai Quality of Life Strategy 2033, while supporting the goals of the Year of the Family 2026. It encouraged families to take part in sporting activities together in a safe and comfortable environment, strengthening family cohesion, establishing physical activity as a way of life and improving quality of life across the community. His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum launched Dubai Mallathon in 2025, with the first edition setting a Guinness World Record for the largest number of participants in a running race inside a shopping mall, with more than 1,300 people taking part in a single race at Dubai Hills Mall.

title: Manal bounces back after failing to make it to u-19 WC team
content:
Manal Chauhan started playing cricket for a simple reason — he wanted to bunk school.
He would tell his parents he was going to school and head off to play cricket instead. “At that time, I was not that interested in the sport, but I kept playing,” Manal told The Hindu ahead of Monday’s second youth ODI between India under-19 and the Australian colts here.
“Gradually, I realised that there were age-group divisions and that you move forward through them and then play for the State. I became very interested in it, so I started giving it my full time.”
The boy from Morena has since led Madhya Pradesh to its maiden Cooch Behar Trophy title and made his India u-19 debut on the Sri Lanka tour, scoring 150 and an unbeaten 51 in the second youth Test.
But it wasn’t a smooth ride. After a decent Vinoo Mankad Trophy campaign, the all-rounder missed out on the u-19 World Cup. “I was very demotivated because I wanted to play the World Cup. At that time, I did not know that there would be further bilateral series like this,” he said.
His parents and coaches told him there would be more opportunities. “I thought that, at least, I would win the red-ball tournament for MP. I did not know that I would come this far from there.”
Madhya Pradesh did win the Cooch Behar Trophy. Then came the India call-up.
“The biggest learning has been that things will keep going up and down in life, but you have to stick to your work ethic,” he said.
Chandrakant Pandit has helped him work on the mental side of the game, while India u-19 coach Yere Goud taught him to forget mistakes and move on.
Manal is doing just that, taking it one step at a time.
Match starts at 9 a.m.

title: ‘Our focus is weakening the Russian army’: For four years, Grigory Sverdlin’s aid group has helped Russians evade the draft and desert
content: In September 2022, immediately after Putin announced “partial” mobilization, Grigory Sverdlin, the former director of Nochlezhka, a foundation that helps the homeless, launched Idite Lesom (“Get Lost”). For four years now, the project has been helping Russians avoid taking part in the war — evading mobilization or deserting. To date, the organization has helped more than 82,000 people. In his book “Punkt Obogreva” (“Warming Station”), which was published by Meduza’s publishing house, Sverdlin describes the launch of Idite Lesom in detail. We are publishing an excerpt from the book about the project’s creation and its earliest days, translated into English.
